words.meaning: An ancient Greek philosophy that teaches self-control and fortitude against adversity.
words.sentence1: His stoicism during the crisis inspired everyone around him. (His stoicism during the crisis inspired everyone around him.)
words.sentence2: She practiced stoicism to remain calm when facing unexpected challenges. (She practiced stoicism to remain calm when facing unexpected challenges.)

words.meaning: A state of serene calmness, untroubled mind, and freedom from emotional disturbance or anxiety.
words.sentence1: Busco la ataraxia a través de la meditación diaria. (I seek ataraxia through daily meditation.)
words.sentence2: El filósofo hablaba de la ataraxia como la meta suprema de la vida. (The philosopher spoke of ataraxia as the supreme goal of life.)

words.meaning: A philosophical concept denoting peace of mind and freedom from mental anxiety.
words.sentence1: Il cherchait l'ataraxie au milieu du chaos de la ville. (He sought ataraxia in the middle of the city's chaos.)
words.sentence2: Cette lecture m'apporte une profonde ataraxie. (This reading brings me a deep sense of ataraxia.)

words.meaning: A particular philosophy or view of life implied by an individual or group.
words.sentence1: Seine Weltanschauung wurde stark von antiken Philosophen geprägt. (His worldview was strongly shaped by ancient philosophers.)
words.sentence2: Jeder Mensch hat eine eigene Weltanschauung. (Every person has their own worldview.)

words.meaning: A philosophical concept of naturalness, spontaneity, and things as they are without artifice.
words.sentence1: Kono niwa wa shizen no utsukushisa o kanji saseru. (This garden makes one feel the beauty of naturalness.)
words.sentence2: Karera wa shizen na kokoro de ikiyou to shita. (They tried to live with a natural and unforced mind.)

words.meaning: Imperturbability of the soul; freedom from mental agitation and passions.
words.sentence1: La ricerca dell'atarassia era fondamentale per i filosofi antichi. (The pursuit of ataraxia was fundamental for ancient philosophers.)
words.sentence2: Egli affrontava ogni problema con una strana atarassia. (He faced every problem with a strange imperturbability.)

words.meaning: An innate moral sense or intuitive knowledge of good and evil in Neo-Confucian philosophy.
words.sentence1: Wang Yangming qiangdiao wuqu xiangxin liangzhi. (Wang Yangming emphasized always trusting one's innate moral sense.)
words.sentence2: Tingcong ni de liangzhi lai zuo jueding. (Listen to your intuitive moral knowledge to make decisions.)

words.meaning: A philosophical state of following nature, truth, and the natural flow of existence.
words.sentence1: Geunyeoneun sunaui gilgeul georeossda. (She walked the path of following nature and truth.)
words.sentence2: Inganui bonseongeun sunawa dahaissda. (Human nature is connected to the concept of natural truth.)

words.meaning: Virtuous disposition, righteousness, or moral excellence in philosophical conduct.
words.sentence1: Kesor cholchett knong kar prampeu sadhuthea. (Kesor loves to practice moral righteousness.)
words.sentence2: Sadhutheachea kruos sa-ngat robos mnuh. (Virtue is the true ornament of a person.)

words.meaning: Equanimity, emotional balance, and steadiness of mind under all circumstances.
words.sentence1: Hy het sy gelyknat behoue te midde van die storm. (He maintained his equanimity amidst the storm.)
words.sentence2: Filosofie help ons om geestelike gelyknat te vind. (Philosophy helps us find mental equanimity.)
